The Rule 26(f) conference must be a meaningful, substantive discussion to build the discovery plan. Parties who do not comply will have no voice at scheduling conferences and may be sanctioned. In criminal cases, follow Fed. R. Crim. P. 16 and the Local Rules of Criminal Procedure.

docs.t: Judge Emile A. Henderson III (D.V.I.) — Settlement, pleas, and motions
docs.x: Judge Emile A. Henderson III, D.V.I.. Settlement, pleas, and motions: Settlement is addressed at all stages, and parties must consider mediation at an appropriate stage, consistent with Local Rule of Civil Procedure 3.2. On settlement, immediately file a notice of settlement, followed by a stipulation of dismissal. In criminal cases, advise the court of any plea as early as possible to avoid unnecessary juror expense. Follow the Local Rules on motion practice. Oral argument may be permitted when unique factual or legal issues are presented.

docs.t: Judge Emile A. Henderson III (D.V.I.) — Trial: scope, schedule, and submissions
docs.x: Judge Emile A. Henderson III, D.V.I.. Trial: scope, schedule, and submissions: The trial policies apply to misdemeanor or criminal trials and to civil cases tried on consent under 28 U.S.C. § 636(c) and Fed. R. Civ. P. 73. Court normally begins at 9:00 a.m.; communication devices are not permitted in the courthouse without a judge’s special permission and may be confiscated. Proposed jury instructions, verdict forms, or special interrogatories are due no later than 10 days before a jury trial, each instruction on a separate page, double spaced, with citations, submitted electronically. In civil cases, proposed voir dire questions are due 10 days before jury selection; the judge conducts voir dire. Peremptory challenges are exercised simultaneously: in a typical two-party civil case 3 per side; in a typical criminal case 6 for the government and 10 for the defendant, with more if alternat

docs.t: Judge Emile A. Henderson III (D.V.I.) — Exhibits and JERS (trap)
docs.x: Judge Emile A. Henderson III, D.V.I.. Exhibits and JERS (trap): Number all exhibits sequentially, regardless of which party offers them, before the proceeding; agreement on admissibility is not required. Prepare exhibit binders for the court and for witnesses, and share every exhibit with the other side before trial. The court uses the Jury Electronic Recording System (JERS): deliver electronic exhibits on a USB flash drive or CD/DVD at least three business days before trial, in the format court technical staff specify, and familiarize yourself with the court’s presentation equipment (including the Elmo document camera) at least three business days before trial. Share any non-court equipment and its instructions with the other side well in advance, and have a backup method ready if the court’s equipment fails.

docs.t: Judge Emile A. Henderson III (D.V.I.) — Depositions, objections, and closings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Emile A. Henderson III, D.V.I.. Depositions, objections, and closings (trap): Designations of deposition or video testimony must be served on all parties no later than two weeks before trial; any unresolved objections must be reported to the court no later than one week before trial. Disputes over the accuracy of recording transcripts must be resolved jointly before trial. Object by saying “objection” and citing the evidentiary rule, without argument unless asked; fuller argument is heard outside the jury’s hearing at a break. In multi-party cases, one party’s objection counts for all unless a party opts out. The court may set time limits for openings and closings. Plaintiff must reserve closing time for rebuttal, or rebuttal may be waived.

docs.t: Judge Andrew M. Edison (S.D. Tex.) — Service of the rules and Rule 16 conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew M. Edison, S.D. Tex.. Service of the rules and Rule 16 conference (trap): Plaintiffs must serve the Galveston Division Rules of Practice on each defendant with the summons and complaint, and a removing party must serve them with the removal papers; proof of service must be filed with the clerk. Judge Edison handles Rule 16 conferences in Galveston; at least one attorney for each represented party must attend. The Joint Discovery/Case Management Plan is due at least 10 days before the conference, and the Rule 26(f) meeting must be in person, by phone, or by video (not by email). The plan must trace the citizenship of every member of a limited liability entity through all layers, and must certify the date each party filed its Disclosure of Interested Parties; do not say it will be filed later. In cases with no obvious factual connection to Galveston, the court will order the p

docs.t: Judge Andrew M. Edison (S.D. Tex.) — Motion format and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew M. Edison, S.D. Tex.. Motion format and page limits (trap): No separate memorandum of law: put the argument in the motion. Double-spaced, 13-point or larger font; motions and responses 30 pages, replies 15 pages, absent leave. A filing with more than 10 pages of argument needs a statement of the nature and stage of the proceeding, a summary of the argument, and a table of authorities. Follow The Bluebook, The Greenbook (which wins over The Bluebook), and The Redbook. Everything represented parties file must be text-searchable PDF, not scanned images. Each exhibit must be separately attached and descriptively labeled in CM/ECF. Audio or video exhibits go to the court on USB drives, not CDs. Every filing may cite only authorities the filer has verified exist; a paper citing a nonexistent case or fabricated quotation or proposition will be struck.

docs.t: Judge Andrew M. Edison (S.D. Tex.) — Briefing deadlines and conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew M. Edison, S.D. Tex.. Briefing deadlines and conference (trap): Responses are due in 21 days and replies within 7 days after the response. Extensions require a motion; an agreement between the parties alone does not extend a deadline. Surreplies and sur-surreplies need leave by motion, are limited to 10 pages, and are struck if unauthorized. A late filing needs a motion for leave explaining why no extension was sought in advance, or it may be struck. Non-dispositive motions without a certificate of conference will be struck. They must include a substantive proposed order (not a bare grant/deny form) with the judge’s signature block; continuance and scheduling motions must propose dates. Motions are decided on the papers, but counsel may request an oral hearing; the case manager gives notice if one is set.

docs.t: Judge Andrew M. Edison (S.D. Tex.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew M. Edison, S.D. Tex.. Discovery disputes (trap): No motion to compel until the parties have first filed a joint letter of no more than 2 pages describing the dispute, each side’s position, and the efforts to resolve it. The court usually then holds a Zoom conference.

docs.t: Judge Andrew M. Edison (S.D. Tex.) — Initial Discovery Protocols
docs.x: Judge Andrew M. Edison, S.D. Tex.. Initial Discovery Protocols: The court requires the posted protocols in premises-liability (slip, trip, or fall), adverse-action employment, individual FLSA, first-party disaster insurance, COVID-19 business-interruption, and residential mortgage cases. They replace Rule 26(a)(1) initial disclosures but do not limit other discovery, and the employment and FLSA protocols must be answered without objections other than privilege and work product. Responses are generally due 30 days after a responsive pleading or motion (or removal, in some protocols); first-party disaster insurance responses are due in 45 days, and in premises cases the defendant responds 14 days after the plaintiff. A court-approved form notice for FLSA collective actions is also posted.

docs.t: Judge Andrew M. Edison (S.D. Tex.) — Sealing and protective order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew M. Edison, S.D. Tex.. Sealing and protective order (trap): The Standing Protective Order allows CONFIDENTIAL and CONFIDENTIAL—ATTORNEYS’ EYES ONLY designations; challenges go to the court if the designating party does not agree within 15 business days, and the designating party bears the burden. Deposition testimony may be designated within 10 business days after receipt of the transcript. Nothing is sealed automatically. The designating party must move to seal with a line-by-line analysis under Binh Hoa Le v. Exeter Fin. Corp.; if another party files designated material under seal, the designating party has 7 days to move or the material is automatically unsealed. Motions to seal must include highlighted proposed redactions, filed with all exhibits as a single combined document, plus public redacted versions. Wholesale sealing requires an extraordinary showing, and agreemen

docs.t: Judge Andrew M. Edison (S.D. Tex.) — Scheduling and continuances
docs.x: Judge Andrew M. Edison, S.D. Tex.. Scheduling and continuances: Parties may agree to extend discovery and expert deadlines without court approval if the dispositive-motion deadline and docket call are unaffected; moving either requires a motion, and agreed motions for continuance do not bind the court. Written discovery is untimely if served so close to the discovery deadline that responses would not be due until after it. After the amendment deadline, leave requires good cause under Rule 16(b)(4); in removed cases, adding parties always requires a motion for leave. A motion to amend must attach a redlined proposed pleading; the clean version must be filed within 14 days after leave is granted, and amended pleadings may not incorporate prior pleadings by reference.

docs.t: Judge Andrew M. Edison (S.D. Tex.) — Docket call and pretrial filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew M. Edison, S.D. Tex.. Docket call and pretrial filings (trap): Docket call (9:30 a.m.) is the final pretrial conference; the court sets trial on a date certain within the next 60 days. No joint pretrial order. At least 24 hours before docket call, each party separately files an exhibit list, witness list, proposed voir dire, proposed jury instructions, motions in limine, and deposition designations and objections, and submits two tabbed binders of those filings and two tabbed binders of exhibits. Exchange limine motions, exhibit lists, and designations at least one week before docket call and confer to narrow issues. Pretrial authenticity and admissibility objections are required under Local Rules 44 and 46 (Rule 11 applies to authenticity objections); the court tries to admit as many exhibits as possible before trial.

docs.t: Judge Andrew M. Edison (S.D. Tex.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Andrew M. Edison, S.D. Tex.. Trial: The court conducts preliminary voir dire; counsel may follow briefly if they properly submitted proposed questions. The court accepts agreements to use a deposition even if the witness is available. Do not tender experts to the court for recognition; all such tenders are refused. Bench trials: proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law are required, and the court may require them before trial or allow post-trial briefs instead of closing argument.

docs.t: Judge Andrew M. Edison (S.D. Tex.) — Emergencies, admiralty, and settlement
docs.x: Judge Andrew M. Edison, S.D. Tex.. Emergencies, admiralty, and settlement: Notify the case manager before filing a TRO, preliminary-injunction, or other emergency motion. For preliminary-injunction hearings, exchange exhibit lists, witness lists, and designations at least 72 hours ahead. Judge Edison rules on all initial ex parte admiralty motions; proposed orders need the judge’s signature block and must also be emailed in Word to the case manager. Tell the case manager when settlement is being discussed so pending motions can be held. Settlement announcements bring a conditional dismissal allowing reinstatement within 60 days; minor-plaintiff settlements with a potential parent conflict require a joint motion for a guardian ad litem.

docs.t: Judge Andrew M. Edison (S.D. Tex.) — Contact and other matters
docs.x: Judge Andrew M. Edison, S.D. Tex.. Contact and other matters: Inquiries in Judge Edison’s cases and about Rule 16 conferences go to the case manager, Vanesa Pacheco (vanesa_pacheco@txs.uscourts.gov). Get docket status from CM/ECF or PACER. Social Security appeals in Galveston must be opened using only the claimant’s initials. A criminal motion to suppress must be filed before the pretrial conference unless otherwise ordered. The page posts a standing ZoomGov link for remote proceedings.

docs.t: Judge Christina Bryan (S.D. Tex.) — Scope
docs.x: Judge Christina Bryan, S.D. Tex.. Scope: The procedures govern cases tried before Judge Bryan on consent and, where applicable, the judge’s criminal docket. In cases or motions referred by a district judge, they apply only to the extent they do not conflict with the referring judge’s procedures.

docs.t: Judge Christina Bryan (S.D. Tex.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christina Bryan, S.D. Tex.. Discovery disputes (trap): Confer by telephone or video first; only then may a party request a conference by filing a letter of no more than 3 pages stating the dispute, the date, time, method, and attendees of the parties’ conference, its outcome, and the relief sought. The court aims to hold the conference within 2–3 business days; any response letter is due at least 24 hours before it. The court tries to resolve disputes at the conference; if a motion is still needed, the issues and briefing schedule are set there. Discovery motions should be filed only after this process fails. Before seeking court help on electronic discovery, the parties must discuss the need for and burden of the search (custodians, time and expense, volume) and options to reduce it, and the resisting party must have someone prepared to explain the specific burdens.

docs.t: Judge Christina Bryan (S.D. Tex.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christina Bryan, S.D. Tex.. Motions (trap): Non-dispositive motions without a Local Rule 7.1(D) certificate of conference are automatically struck. All motions are limited to 25 double-spaced pages, 12-point font, 1-inch margins, without leave. Most motions are decided on submission. Requests for oral hearing and for expedited consideration must each be filed separately from the motion. The court may shorten a response deadline; a party may move to extend the shortened date. Opposed extension motions are considered only if timely filed. You may ask the case manager about the status of a civil motion that has been ripe for more than 60 days.

docs.t: Judge Christina Bryan (S.D. Tex.) — Courtesy copies and voluminous exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christina Bryan, S.D. Tex.. Courtesy copies and voluminous exhibits (trap): Courtesy copies are generally not required. But if exhibits exceed 50 pages, singly or combined, file them as a single PDF bookmarked by exhibit and to the cited portions, highlight the referenced parts of voluminous exhibits, and give the same PDF to opposing counsel. If you use a PowerPoint at oral argument, give printed copies to the court and opposing counsel at the hearing.

docs.t: Judge Christina Bryan (S.D. Tex.) — Appearances and Rule 16 conference
docs.x: Judge Christina Bryan, S.D. Tex.. Appearances and Rule 16 conference: Before the Rule 16 conference, hold the Rule 26(f) meeting, make initial disclosures, file the Joint Discovery/Case Management Plan, and submit a proposed Scheduling and Docket Control Order. Be ready to discuss every aspect of the case; the court may hear and rule on pending motions at the conference. In-person appearance is preferred. Requests to appear by telephone or video must be made in writing to the case manager at least 3 days ahead; video is available only if all parties appear by video. Join at least 5 minutes early. Appearing counsel must know the case, have authority to bind the client, and be in charge. The court encourages speaking roles for lawyers licensed fewer than 7 years. Pro hac vice motions must aver that the applicant is familiar with the Local Rules and these procedures.

docs.t: Judge Christina Bryan (S.D. Tex.) — Scheduling order
docs.x: Judge Christina Bryan, S.D. Tex.. Scheduling order: Defense experts are due within 30 days after the deposition of plaintiff’s last expert, but no later than the date set. Counsel may agree to continue discovery past the deadline, but the court will not intervene and no continuance will be granted based on post-deadline discovery. The Joint Pretrial Order must be filed by its deadline even if a continuance motion is pending; failure to file it timely subjects the case to dismissal with prejudice. Motions in limine are submitted with it. The pretrial conference is at 2:00 p.m. and trial at 9:30 a.m.; depositions for a bench trial go to chambers at least 5 days before trial. On consent, an existing scheduling order may be vacated and replaced; consent cases get a date-certain trial setting.

docs.t: Judge Christina Bryan (S.D. Tex.) — Continuances
docs.x: Judge Christina Bryan, S.D. Tex.. Continuances: Motions for continuance are considered if filed at least 2 weeks before the trial date; responses are due at least 1 week before trial. Agreed continuances do not bind the court and must be submitted as an agreed or unopposed motion with a proposed order.

docs.t: Judge Christina Bryan (S.D. Tex.) — Pretrial order and jury charge
docs.x: Judge Christina Bryan, S.D. Tex.. Pretrial order and jury charge: The Joint Pretrial Order follows Local Rule 16.2, Appendix B, and must include proposed voir dire questions and page-and-line deposition designations, with objections and authority filed with it. Plaintiff’s counsel must file it and deliver a courtesy copy with all attachments; if plaintiff does not file, defendant must file its portion. Submit a single unified jury charge (to the case manager in Word), each instruction numbered with authority, following the Fifth Circuit or Texas pattern charges where possible; label each disputed item by requesting party and justify any deviation from the pattern. Bench trials: proposed conclusions of law must cite authority, and findings must cite supporting testimony and exhibits, supplemented at the close of each trial day; submit them in Word.

docs.t: Judge Christina Bryan (S.D. Tex.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Christina Bryan, S.D. Tex.. Trial: Trial hours are generally 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; tell the case manager in advance if a long day will cause child-care or similar hardship. Counsel generally conduct voir dire after the court’s opening remarks, subject to time limits. Mark exhibits to match the pretrial-order list and provide tabbed, indexed exhibit notebooks for the court and the witness. The court tries to rule on exhibit objections at the final pretrial conference or before trial starts; ask permission before passing an exhibit to the jury. Provide one copy of each deposition used at trial with color-coded highlighting for each party’s excerpts. State the evidence rule when objecting and do not argue rulings before the jury. Reserve witness rooms with the case manager the week before trial.

docs.t: Judge Christina Bryan (S.D. Tex.) — Contact and courtroom
docs.x: Judge Christina Bryan, S.D. Tex.. Contact and courtroom: Case inquiries go only to the case manager, Melissa Morgan (713-250-5860), never the law clerks. Do not raise substantive issues by phone or email; substantive letters must be filed, and emails to the case manager may be docketed. Counsel may examine from counsel table or the podium. Counsel may use electronic devices at counsel table after asking permission; video and audio exhibits go on a labeled thumb drive or disc. Notify the court immediately of a settlement; the court may enter a 30- or 60-day conditional dismissal. Defendants not served within 90 days may be dismissed under Rule 4(m).

docs.t: Judge Juan F. Alanis (S.D. Tex.) — Presiding judge’s rules control (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan F. Alanis, S.D. Tex.. Presiding judge’s rules control (trap): In both civil and criminal cases, Judge Alanis adopts the procedural rules of the presiding judge for the case, on top of the Local Rules. Check the district judge’s procedures too.

docs.t: Judge Juan F. Alanis (S.D. Tex.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan F. Alanis, S.D. Tex.. Courtesy copies (trap): Any submission over 50 pages, including motions, briefs, and attachments, requires a courtesy hard copy filed with the District Clerk’s Office.

docs.t: Judge Juan F. Alanis (S.D. Tex.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge Juan F. Alanis, S.D. Tex.. Motions: The court follows the Local Rules’ written motion practice. Counsel and pro se parties must make serious and timely efforts to confer, and every motion needs a certificate of conference stating whether it is opposed and a separate proposed order. Opposed motions may be decided without notice once 21 days have passed after filing. Joint motions for continuance do not bind the court.

docs.t: Judge Juan F. Alanis (S.D. Tex.) — Appearances
docs.x: Judge Juan F. Alanis, S.D. Tex.. Appearances: Appearing counsel must be admitted in the court, familiar with the case, authorized to bind the client, and in charge, and must be ready to discuss any pending motion or issue at any setting. Telephone conferences are allowed only in limited circumstances, on a motion that states all parties agree to appear by telephone. Notify the case manager immediately if a matter set for trial or hearing is resolved.

docs.t: Judge Juan F. Alanis (S.D. Tex.) — Contact with chambers
docs.x: Judge Juan F. Alanis, S.D. Tex.. Contact with chambers: Communicate through the case manager, Nelida Campos (956-618-8478), including on criminal matters; ex parte contact through the law clerk is strictly forbidden, and the law clerk will not discuss cases or procedures. Get filing and docket information from the District Clerk. Do not raise substantive issues by letter, and file copies of all case-related letters via CM/ECF. Do not fax documents to the judge without prior approval.

docs.t: Judge Juan F. Alanis (S.D. Tex.) — Courtroom
docs.x: Judge Juan F. Alanis, S.D. Tex.. Courtroom: Formal etiquette under Appendix C of the Local Rules and formal attire are required; counsel must tell witnesses and family members about the attire rule. Stand when addressing the court. Phones, laptops, and other wireless devices may not be used in the courtroom without the judge’s approval.

docs.t: Judge Juan F. Alanis (S.D. Tex.) — Settlement and dismissal
docs.x: Judge Juan F. Alanis, S.D. Tex.. Settlement and dismissal: Parties in every civil case must make a good-faith effort to settle. Rule 41(a) is strictly applied: once an adverse party has answered, the plaintiff may dismiss only by a stipulation signed by all parties who have appeared.

docs.t: Judge Julie K. Hampton (S.D. Tex.) — Applicability and service (trap)
docs.x: Judge Julie K. Hampton, S.D. Tex.. Applicability and service (trap): The procedures apply to all civil and criminal cases assigned to Judge Hampton except prisoner civil rights, habeas, agency appeals, miscellaneous government cases, and miscellaneous matters. Strict compliance is required, and they control over the Local Rules on any inconsistency. Plaintiff must formally serve the procedures with the summons and complaint (with the Order for Scheduling Conference) and file proof of service. A removing party must file a certificate of service and a Statement of Information in Removed Action (Form 1: service dates, citizenship of all parties including every LLC or partnership member, amount in controversy, and nonjoining defendants) within 10 days of removal, or the case may be summarily remanded.

docs.t: Judge Julie K. Hampton (S.D. Tex.) — Briefing format and word limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Julie K. Hampton, S.D. Tex.. Briefing format and word limits (trap): No separate memorandum of law. Motions and responses are limited to 5,000 words and replies to 2,000 words, with a certificate of word count after the signature block; no surreply without permission. Minimum 12-point font, 1-inch margins, double-spaced. The court disregards evidence or argument raised only in a footnote. Every motion needs a summary of the argument, a statement of facts, argument, a conclusion stating the precise relief, and headings; one with more than 10 pages of argument also needs a table of contents, categorized table of authorities, introduction, and point headings. Give pinpoint cites to authority and evidence (Bates numbers where available). File each exhibit separately with a cover sheet and a descriptive docket label, and append any authority not on Westlaw or Lexis.

docs.t: Judge Julie K. Hampton (S.D. Tex.) — Motions and conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Julie K. Hampton, S.D. Tex.. Motions and conference (trap): Civil motions without a certificate of conference are struck (criminal ones may be). Before a Rule 12(b)(6) or 12(c) motion on a claim or counterclaim, identify the deficiencies to the other side and confer about curing them by amendment; the certificate must say so, or the motion is struck. Opposed civil motions are considered 28 days after filing; responses are due in 21 days and replies within 7 days of the response. Request expedited decision, oral argument, or advise of an agreed extension by email or letter. Non-dispositive motions and oppositions need a proposed order (Form 5). Most motions are decided on the papers. The court weighs in favor of oral argument when a young lawyer who substantially drafted the papers will argue. Email the court immediately if a pending motion is resolved.

docs.t: Judge Julie K. Hampton (S.D. Tex.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Julie K. Hampton, S.D. Tex.. Courtesy copies (trap): Promptly submit courtesy copies of documents of 50 pages or more (including exhibits), all sealed filings regardless of length, filings on matters to be heard within 7 days, and joint pretrial orders and trial materials. Copies over 50 pages must be double-sided in binders no larger than 4 inches with right-margin tabs, bearing the CM/ECF file stamp, and mailed or hand-delivered to the case manager with a transmittal letter (not filed; send it to the other parties without attachments).

docs.t: Judge Julie K. Hampton (S.D. Tex.) — Discovery disputes and privilege logs (trap)
docs.x: Judge Julie K. Hampton, S.D. Tex.. Discovery disputes and privilege logs (trap): Lead counsel must personally confer. No discovery or scheduling motion without permission: send a letter of about 2 single-spaced pages describing the dispute, the lead-counsel conference, and its results; the opponent may respond briefly, and no reply is allowed. The court may rule on the letters or set a conference. No letter is needed for relief against a nonparty. In electronic-data disputes, each side must have someone with detailed knowledge of the systems at the conference. A party may once request in camera review of up to 20 documents for privilege-log misuse, by letter of about 3 single-spaced pages after lead counsel confer, at least 60 days before discovery closes (or promptly after a later log); the letter consents to ex parte contact with the opponent about the privilege.

docs.t: Judge Julie K. Hampton (S.D. Tex.) — Discovery rules
docs.x: Judge Julie K. Hampton, S.D. Tex.. Discovery rules: Start initial disclosures immediately, including copies of the documents. Discovery may begin by agreement once all defendants are served. No preambles, general or boilerplate objections, or “to the extent” objections; say what is withheld under each objection and give a deadline for any promised supplementation. Tactical late supplementation may lead to striking evidence, witnesses, claims, or pleadings. ESI is produced natively or in a usable common format and is initially limited to 5 custodians chosen by the requesting party. Plaintiff presumptively takes the first deposition and the sides then alternate; number deposition exhibits sequentially across all depositions and use each exhibit’s single number at trial.

docs.t: Judge Julie K. Hampton (S.D. Tex.) — Scheduling, emergencies, and sealing
docs.x: Judge Julie K. Hampton, S.D. Tex.. Scheduling, emergencies, and sealing: The scheduling order changes only on a motion showing good cause, with proposed dates for all later deadlines; parties may agree to extend discovery deadlines that do not affect court-set dates. Form 3 requires the joint plan 14 days and interested-party disclosures 15 days before the scheduling conference. Ex parte TROs require Rule 65(b) compliance; file on CM/ECF, attempt immediate informal service, and confirm in writing to the case manager that the opponent was contacted and all parties are available for a conference. Email emergency motions to the case manager after filing; extension motions are not emergencies. Protective orders are entered on a joint or opposed motion after conferring. To seal, file the material under seal with a descriptive title plus “(SEALED),” and separately file a public motion to seal

docs.t: Judge Julie K. Hampton (S.D. Tex.) — Pretrial filings and exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Julie K. Hampton, S.D. Tex.. Pretrial filings and exhibits (trap): With the Joint Pretrial Order (Form 6, signed by all lead counsel), each party files exhibit and witness lists, deposition designations, motions in limine, proposed voir dire, a jury charge or proposed findings and conclusions, and a trial memorandum of law. Plaintiff or the prosecution delivers three copies of a joint trial notebook at least 4 business days before trial. Exhibit and witness objections, with authority, are due within 2 calendar days of listing and exchange (superseding the Local Rule time limits), responses 2 days later; submit all exhibits on a USB drive plus three copies. Demonstratives must be disclosed by 10:00 p.m. the night before use. Deposition designations are presumptively limited to 25 minutes and counter-designations to 15 minutes, and the court usually refuses them for available party w

docs.t: Judge Julie K. Hampton (S.D. Tex.) — Jury charge and bench trials
docs.x: Judge Julie K. Hampton, S.D. Tex.. Jury charge and bench trials: Civil parties file a joint or unified charge using the Fifth Circuit pattern instructions, numbered and supported, with disputed language in bold or italics and no argument in footnotes; plaintiff also submits a Word version. In criminal cases, the prosecution’s pattern-based charge and the defense objections are due 3 working days before the final pretrial conference. Bench trials require proposed findings with evidentiary cites, proposed conclusions with authority, and a memorandum of law, followed by supplemental findings and conclusions citing the trial record.

docs.t: Judge Julie K. Hampton (S.D. Tex.) — Trial and courtroom
docs.x: Judge Julie K. Hampton, S.D. Tex.. Trial and courtroom: The jury is typically seated at 9:00 a.m. and adjourns shortly after 5:00 p.m.; there may be no trial on Fridays. Docket call may serve as the final pretrial conference, and civil cases are set on a trailing docket. Question witnesses from the lectern or counsel table and ask leave to approach. The court will not recess for missing witnesses (unless subpoenaed) or interpreters, or for technical problems caused by lack of testing. Phones must be off; laptops are allowed before the bar for litigation only. Contact chambers only through the case manager, Melissa Arguello (361-888-3432); never initiate contact with law clerks. Copy all parties on any letter or email and do not file them. Pro hac vice applications must aver familiarity with the procedures, and are not to be sought for Corpus Christi-area attorneys.

docs.t: Judge Julie K. Hampton (S.D. Tex.) — Settlement and remote access
docs.x: Judge Julie K. Hampton, S.D. Tex.. Settlement and remote access: Tell the court by letter or email when serious settlement talks are under way (pending motions will be postponed) and immediately by email on settlement. Minor settlements with a parent conflict require a joint motion for a guardian ad litem hearing. The page posts a standing ZoomGov link; the division’s Zoom order requires business attire, a quiet private location, and no recording, forwarding of invitations, or rebroadcast.

docs.t: Judge Mitchel Neurock (S.D. Tex.) — Applicability
docs.x: Judge Mitchel Neurock, S.D. Tex.. Applicability: The manual governs civil cases in which all parties consented to Judge Neurock and civil cases or matters referred by a district judge; on a referred matter, the district judge’s conflicting procedures control. It does not apply to prisoner civil rights, habeas, or Social Security appeals (which proceed under case orders), though it also gives Social Security briefing rules. Noncompliant filings may be struck under LR 11.4, and a case-specific order controls over the manual.

docs.t: Judge Mitchel Neurock (S.D. Tex.) — Conferring out loud (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mitchel Neurock, S.D. Tex.. Conferring out loud (trap): Before any motion, and before contacting the court about any dispute, counsel must confer by telephone, video, or in person; letters, emails, and voicemails are not enough. All motions except those under Rule 12(b), (c), (e), or (f) or Rule 56 need a certificate of conference saying whether relief is opposed. If the other side never responded, the certificate must describe at least two attempts, with date, time, and method. Motions without the certificate may be struck.

docs.t: Judge Mitchel Neurock (S.D. Tex.) — Pre-motion conference for discovery and scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mitchel Neurock, S.D. Tex.. Pre-motion conference for discovery and scheduling (trap): Any motion on a discovery or scheduling dispute (to compel, quash, for protection, for sanctions, and similar) is struck if filed before a pre-motion conference; disputes with nonparties are excepted. Request the conference by email to the case manager, Annette Martinez (annette_martinez@txs.uscourts.gov), in under 200 words: the dispute and relief sought, the date, time, method, and participants of the conference, and its result, with the discovery request and response attached; no case law or argument. A response email of no more than 200 words is due at least 24 hours before the conference; no replies. The judge may resolve the dispute on the emails or set a hearing, usually by video, and sets issues and briefing if a motion is still needed. For ESI disputes, each side must have someone with d

docs.t: Judge Mitchel Neurock (S.D. Tex.) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mitchel Neurock, S.D. Tex.. Motions and briefing (trap): No separate memorandum of law. Motions and responses are limited to 5,000 words, replies and court-requested supplemental briefs to 2,000 words, counting headings and footnotes; every brief needs a certificate of word count after the signature block. Filings over 2,500 words need tables of contents and authorities. Opposed motions are submitted 21 days after filing, and a response must be filed by then; no response is taken as no opposition. Replies are due 7 days after the response, surreplies need leave, and the judge may not wait for replies or may shorten response times. Every motion needs a separate proposed order not titled “proposed”; unopposed motions and their orders must say “Unopposed” in the caption. Requests for expedited consideration and for oral argument must each be filed separately with reasons; nearly all m

docs.t: Judge Mitchel Neurock (S.D. Tex.) — Communications with chambers
docs.x: Judge Mitchel Neurock, S.D. Tex.. Communications with chambers: Direct all case calls and emails to the case manager and copy all parties; emails after 5 p.m. CT may not be seen until the next business day. Never contact the judge or law clerk directly. Do not raise substance by phone or email or send letter briefs; seek substantive relief only by motion. Do not ask about the status of pending motions unless circumstances make one more urgent. Emergencies are rare, and extension motions are not emergencies. File on CM/ECF, then email the case manager copying all parties; ex parte applications must satisfy Rule 65(b), and the movant must confirm in writing that the opponent was contacted and all parties are available, or explain why not.

docs.t: Judge Mitchel Neurock (S.D. Tex.) — Appearances and videoconference
docs.x: Judge Mitchel Neurock, S.D. Tex.. Appearances and videoconference: Only counsel of record on the docket may appear. The attorney-in-charge must attend every setting or send a fully informed attorney with authority. Pro hac vice motions must state the applicant has read the Local Rules and the manual. Withdrawal motions must state the client’s position and list all pending deadlines and settings. Many hearings are by video, but evidentiary hearings and trials are in person unless ordered otherwise. To switch formats, email the case manager, copying all parties, at least 3 business days ahead with reasons. Join video settings at least 10 minutes early, camera on. The judge encourages speaking roles for lawyers licensed fewer than 7 years.

docs.t: Judge Mitchel Neurock (S.D. Tex.) — Initial conference and disclosures
docs.x: Judge Mitchel Neurock, S.D. Tex.. Initial conference and disclosures: Before the initial pretrial conference (normally by video), confer under Rule 26(f), make initial disclosures, discuss ADR, and file the district’s joint discovery/case management plan, which must address handling of withheld privileged material under Rule 26(b)(5)(A). The judge may hear and rule on pending motions there. In diversity cases every party must file, on first appearance, a statement identifying the citizenship of every person or entity whose citizenship is attributed to it, including each LLC member and partner. Notify the court of related cases and directly affected nonparties.

docs.t: Judge Mitchel Neurock (S.D. Tex.) — Continuances
docs.x: Judge Mitchel Neurock, S.D. Tex.. Continuances: Agreements between counsel do not bind the court, though agreed requests are liberally granted. A motion must state the current and proposed dates, the specific reason, the number of prior extensions, proposed dates for all affected deadlines, and each party’s position. Out-of-time requests are disfavored. Motions to continue trial must be filed at least 2 weeks before the setting, with any response at least 1 week before. Trial settings are firm; a conflicting setting is no ground unless counsel has actually begun trial elsewhere.

docs.t: Judge Mitchel Neurock (S.D. Tex.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Mitchel Neurock, S.D. Tex.. Discovery: No preambles, general or boilerplate objections, “to the extent” objections, or “subject to” or “without waiving” responses; state whether anything is withheld, and give a date for any promised later production. Restate each request before its response. No more than 25 interrogatories, counting subparts, without leave. Number deposition exhibits sequentially across all depositions and reuse each number at trial. A protective order does not authorize sealed filing. To seal, file provisionally under seal and, at the same time, publicly move for leave explaining why each portion should be sealed, with a proposed redacted version; docket it with a descriptive title followed by “(Sealed).”

docs.t: Judge Mitchel Neurock (S.D. Tex.) — Pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge Mitchel Neurock, S.D. Tex.. Pretrial and trial: Plaintiff files the Joint Pretrial Order (LR Appendix B); if plaintiff fails, defendant must file its portions. With it, each party files exhibit and witness lists, page-and-line deposition designations, motions in limine with proposed orders, and voir dire and a joint proposed charge (jury) or proposed findings and conclusions (bench). Exchange all exhibits before the pretrial order is filed. Authentication challenges are due in writing within 7 days after listing, and admissibility objections with authority at least 7 days before trial. Limine responses are due in 7 days; no boilerplate or bench-trial limine motions. File a single unified jury charge using Fifth Circuit patterns, with disputed items in bold, underline, or italics (not color), and email a Word version to the case manager; do the same with bench-trial findings. At lea

docs.t: Judge Mitchel Neurock (S.D. Tex.) — Settlement, mediation, and Social Security
docs.x: Judge Mitchel Neurock, S.D. Tex.. Settlement, mediation, and Social Security: Notify the court immediately of a settlement affecting a setting by email to the case manager (copying all parties) and file a notice. Minor settlements with a parent conflict require a joint motion for a guardian ad litem and approval hearing. In consent cases, mediation is before a different magistrate judge; trial counsel and a representative with full authority (and any insurer) must attend mediations. Social Security appeals use the claimant’s first name and last initial in every caption; every factual assertion needs a record-page cite, and the plaintiff’s brief must begin with a numbered statement of issues.

docs.t: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho (S.D. Tex.) — Scope (trap)
docs.x: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho, S.D. Tex.. Scope (trap): Since February 5, 2025, the procedures govern all cases referred by a district judge for full pretrial management, as well as all consent cases. They supplement, and do not supersede, the Local Rules and Federal Rules; noncompliance may draw sanctions.

docs.t: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho (S.D. Tex.) — Brief format and word limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho, S.D. Tex.. Brief format and word limits (trap): No separate memorandum of law. Briefs must be in 13-point proportionally spaced font (12-point footnotes), double-spaced, 1-inch margins, and fully justified. Put no citations to authorities or exhibits in footnotes, and minimize footnotes. Primary briefs are limited to 6,500 words and replies to 2,500 words, counting headings and footnotes; every brief needs a certificate of word-count compliance. Except in habeas, prisoner, and Social Security cases, briefs over 10 pages must contain, in this order: table of contents, table of authorities, statement of issues, standard of review, summary of the argument, argument with descriptive headings, a short conclusion stating the precise relief, and certificates.

docs.t: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho (S.D. Tex.) — Certificates and proposed orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho, S.D. Tex.. Certificates and proposed orders (trap): All motions except summary-judgment motions need a certificate of conference stating whether relief is opposed; if no response was obtained, it must show at least two attempts, with the number, method, date, and time. All filings need a certificate of service. A filing missing any required certificate (conference, service, or word count) will be stricken. All motions except summary-judgment motions need a separate proposed order not titled “proposed.”

docs.t: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho (S.D. Tex.) — Discovery and scheduling disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho, S.D. Tex.. Discovery and scheduling disputes (trap): No motion on a discovery or scheduling issue without the pre-motion conference process. After conferring in good faith, file a joint letter, labeled as a motion for pre-motion conference, of no more than 3 pages identifying the disputes, with no case law or argument. The letter must state the date, time, and place of the parties’ discussions, the result, and the names of all participants. The court may rule on the letter or hold a conference, and decides whether and when written submissions are filed.

docs.t: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho (S.D. Tex.) — Briefing deadlines and oral argument
docs.x: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho, S.D. Tex.. Briefing deadlines and oral argument: Responses must be filed before the motion is submitted on the 21st day after filing; replies are due within 7 days after the response. No further briefing without leave, which is disfavored, and the court may rule before the response deadline when circumstances dictate. Counsel are invited to request oral hearings. In deciding whether to hear a motion usually decided on the papers, the court considers whether a less experienced attorney who worked on the motion will argue.

docs.t: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho (S.D. Tex.) — Contact and emergencies
docs.x: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho, S.D. Tex.. Contact and emergencies: Case inquiries go only to the case manager, Rachel Willborg (713-250-5725, Rachel_Willborg@txs.uscourts.gov); do not contact the law clerks or the judge. The case manager will not answer casual status inquiries. Copy all counsel and pro se parties on all correspondence; emails may be docketed, and any request for relief by email is disregarded without notice. Documents delivered after 5:00 p.m. may not be reviewed until the next business day. File applications for immediate relief on CM/ECF, then contact the case manager (copying opponents); they are presented only after counsel affirms the opponent was contacted and both sides can attend a conference, or explains why not. Extension motions are not emergencies.

docs.t: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho (S.D. Tex.) — Appearances and initial conference
docs.x: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho, S.D. Tex.. Appearances and initial conference: Only attorneys of record on the docket may appear; signing a filing is not an appearance. Appearing counsel must know the case, be ready to argue pending motions, and have authority to bind the client. The initial pretrial conference is by video unless a party timely requests in person; no telephone appearances there. Out-of-town counsel may request telephone appearance at other settings by email well in advance, though the court prefers in-person or video hearings on dispositive or contested motions. File the district’s joint discovery/case management plan, signed by all parties and filed by plaintiff, with a proposed scheduling order on Form A. Pro hac vice motions must aver familiarity with the Local Rules and these procedures, and are not to be sought for Houston-area attorneys.

docs.t: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho (S.D. Tex.) — Continuances and sealing
docs.x: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho, S.D. Tex.. Continuances and sealing: Agreed motions or stipulations for continuance do not bind the court. Trial settings are usually firm: continuances are rarely granted for discovery disputes, never because a witness is unavailable, and the court will not continue a trial setting unless counsel has begun trial in another court. Form A’s motions deadline cannot be changed without leave. A party may file provisionally under seal but must contemporaneously move for leave to seal; the court may direct a public redacted version.

docs.t: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho (S.D. Tex.) — Pretrial filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho, S.D. Tex.. Pretrial filings (trap): Plaintiff files the joint pretrial order (Form B) by the scheduling-order deadline; if plaintiff fails, defendant files its portions. Late filing risks sanctions including dismissal for want of prosecution. The same day, each party separately files an exhibit list, objections to opposing exhibits, a witness list, deposition designations, a memorandum of law on contested legal issues, proposed voir dire questions, and motions in limine; limine responses are due within 7 days. Jury cases also need a single joint proposed charge and a separate joint verdict form, with authority in footnotes and disputed items in bold, underline, or italics (not color), and Word copies emailed to the case manager. Bench trials: each party files proposed findings and conclusions with the pretrial order. At least 4 days before trial, jointly submit two do

docs.t: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho (S.D. Tex.) — Docket call, exhibits, and trial
docs.x: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho, S.D. Tex.. Docket call, exhibits, and trial: Docket call is generally the first Friday of each month (Form A: 1:30 p.m., Courtroom 704; trial starts at 9:00 a.m.). Be ready to address all pending motions and disputed issues; a separate final pretrial conference may be set. Pre-mark exhibits with party name, case number, and exhibit number, and exchange them before the pretrial order is filed. Listed exhibits may be admitted unless specific written objections with authority are filed at least 7 days before trial; deposition-designation objections are also due 7 days before trial. The court tries to pre-admit exhibits. Only exhibits admitted and actually used go to the jury; counsel, not court staff, keep custody of exhibits and must check them each day. The court conducts preliminary voir dire, and counsel may follow briefly if questions were timely submitted.

docs.t: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho (S.D. Tex.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Yvonne Y. Ho, S.D. Tex.. Settlement: In consent cases, the court can refer the case on request to mediation before a different magistrate judge. Notify the case manager in writing immediately on settlement; the court may enter a conditional dismissal.

docs.t: Judge William E. Duffin (E.D. Wis.) — Contacting the court (trap)
docs.x: Judge William E. Duffin, E.D. Wis.. Contacting the court (trap): Avoid calling chambers. Scheduling, filing, and docketing questions go to the judge’s deputy clerks in the Clerk’s office: 414-297-3798 for cases ending in an even number and 414-297-3996 for cases ending in an odd number. Have your case number ready; the deputy clerks will transfer you to chambers staff if needed. DuffinPO@wied.uscourts.gov is only for proposed orders and documents related to mediations the judge conducts; do not use it for other inquiries or correspondence. Telephonic hearings: call 669-254-5252, enter meeting ID 160 9647 6949# and # again, then passcode 943682#.

docs.t: Judge William E. Duffin (E.D. Wis.) — Requests for court action (trap)
docs.x: Judge William E. Duffin, E.D. Wis.. Requests for court action (trap): If you want the court to do anything, file a motion, not a letter, notice, or stipulation, even for a joint request; otherwise the request may not be routed properly and action may be delayed. Extensions: ask the other side whether it opposes, then file an expedited motion under Civ. L.R. 7(h) stating whether the request is opposed. Do not wait until the last day.

docs.t: Judge William E. Duffin (E.D. Wis.) — Amended pleadings
docs.x: Judge William E. Duffin, E.D. Wis.. Amended pleadings: Before moving to amend under Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a)(2), consult every represented party about whether the motion is opposed. If it is unopposed, provide written consent so the amended pleading can be filed without a motion.

docs.t: Judge William E. Duffin (E.D. Wis.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge William E. Duffin, E.D. Wis.. Discovery disputes (trap): Try to work it out first. A party may file a motion requesting a telephonic conference if it might avoid a formal discovery motion, but the judge’s role there is largely to help the parties agree. To get a ruling on a dispute (and an award of fees and expenses), you must file a motion to compel.

docs.t: Judge William E. Duffin (E.D. Wis.) — Sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge William E. Duffin, E.D. Wis.. Sealing (trap): Beyond complying with Gen. L.R. 79(d), seal only the confidential portions: publicly file a redacted version and file the unredacted version under seal. A document with some confidential sections generally should not be sealed in its entirety, and filers are responsible for effective redaction. Sealed documents must be served on the other parties in paper, because parties do not receive them electronically.

docs.t: Judge William E. Duffin (E.D. Wis.) — Paper copies and oral argument
docs.x: Judge William E. Duffin, E.D. Wis.. Paper copies and oral argument: The judge generally does not need paper copies of filings; staff will ask if one is needed. Oral argument is rare and set only if the judge thinks it appropriate; nearly all motions are decided on the briefs.

docs.t: Judge William E. Duffin (E.D. Wis.) — Brief writing preferences
docs.x: Judge William E. Duffin, E.D. Wis.. Brief writing preferences: Follow The Bluebook and put citations in the text, not in footnotes. Limit footnotes, and do not try to reserve or advance an argument in a footnote. Give e-filed attachments descriptive names (for example, “Ex. A – 2015 Sales Figures,” not “Attachment 1”), and do not resubmit an exhibit another party already filed, such as a deposition attached to the opposing summary judgment motion. Motions to strike are disfavored and should be reserved for extraordinary circumstances.

docs.t: Judge William E. Duffin (E.D. Wis.) — In the courtroom
docs.x: Judge William E. Duffin, E.D. Wis.. In the courtroom: Counsel may stand or sit when addressing the court or questioning a witness, but must speak into a microphone because hearings are audio recorded and the record will otherwise be incomplete. No permission is needed to approach a witness briefly; return to the podium or counsel table to continue questioning. Water bottles and covered beverages are allowed.

docs.t: Judge William E. Duffin (E.D. Wis.) — Pro se parties
docs.x: Judge William E. Duffin, E.D. Wis.. Pro se parties: Serve every filing on a pro se litigant in paper and file a certificate of service, because pro se litigants are not on the electronic filing system. A summary judgment motion (or a Rule 12(b)(6) or (c) motion presenting matters outside the pleadings) against a pro se party must comply with Civil L.R. 56(a).

docs.t: Judge Amy Potter (D. Or.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Amy Potter, D. Or.. Discovery disputes (trap): Discovery is handled informally and formal motions to compel are discouraged. For a dispute, jointly email the courtroom deputy; the matter will be quickly set for a telephonic hearing. If you expect to need help with a deposition dispute, tell the courtroom deputy the deposition date and time in advance.

docs.t: Judge Amy Potter (D. Or.) — Judge’s copies
docs.x: Judge Amy Potter, D. Or.. Judge’s copies: Judge Potter waives LR 5-10 and requires no paper copies except as noted in the Trial Management Order. The waiver does not apply to documents in the judge’s cases that another judge will consider, unless that judge also waives the rule.

docs.t: Judge Amy Potter (D. Or.) — Motion hearings
docs.x: Judge Amy Potter, D. Or.. Motion hearings: Oral argument on dispositive motions is generally permitted when requested, preferably in person. Video or telephone argument requires good cause (for example, significant travel expense, health and safety concerns, or unavoidable scheduling conflicts). To request argument, contact the courtroom deputy and include any request for phone or video.

docs.t: Judge Amy Potter (D. Or.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Amy Potter, D. Or.. Summary judgment: Seek summary judgment only on issues with no question of material fact or that raise significant dispositive legal issues. Cite the record by paragraph number of affidavits and declarations or by page number of deposition excerpts, and submit all documents in an organized fashion.

docs.t: Judge Amy Potter (D. Or.) — Rule 16 and expedited cases
docs.x: Judge Amy Potter, D. Or.. Rule 16 and expedited cases: Rule 16 conferences are set after all defendants have answered. Confer under Rule 26(f) beforehand and be ready to discuss scheduling; emailing a joint proposed case management schedule to the courtroom deputy in advance is encouraged. If the parties consent to a magistrate judge and agree to an expedited schedule, the court sets a case management conference on discovery limits and dispositive motions and will try to set trial within six months of that conference.

docs.t: Judge Amy Potter (D. Or.) — Young lawyers
docs.x: Judge Amy Potter, D. Or.. Young lawyers: The judge strongly encourages giving lawyers practicing less than 7 years speaking roles (oral argument and witness examination) alongside experienced counsel, especially when they drafted the papers. An experienced attorney may supplement their arguments and questions.

docs.t: Judge Amy Potter (D. Or.) — Settlement, courtroom, and contact
docs.x: Judge Amy Potter, D. Or.. Settlement, courtroom, and contact: Request settlement conferences through the courtroom deputy (541-431-4102). The proposed-documents email is only for jury instructions and proposed orders under LR 5, not filings. Under LR 83-14, wireless devices must be silent in the courthouse, and nothing may be recorded, including remote proceedings. Give advance notice of teleconferencing, video display, or other technology needs. Pro hac vice counsel and their Oregon counsel should know the Local Rules and the 2013 Federal Bar Association newsletter article “The Integral Role of Local Counsel in the District of Oregon,” which stresses that local counsel must “meaningfully participate” (LR 83-3(a)(1)).

docs.t: Judge Andrew D. Hallman (D. Or.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew D. Hallman, D. Or.. Discovery disputes (trap): Discovery is handled informally and formal motions to compel are discouraged. For a dispute, jointly email the courtroom deputy; the matter will be quickly set for a telephonic hearing. If you expect to need help with a deposition dispute, tell the courtroom deputy the deposition date and time in advance.

docs.t: Judge Andrew D. Hallman (D. Or.) — Motion hearings and judge’s copies
docs.x: Judge Andrew D. Hallman, D. Or.. Motion hearings and judge’s copies: Oral argument on dispositive motions is generally permitted, preferably in person at the Kilkenny Courthouse in Pendleton (not staffed). Video or telephone argument requires good cause (for example, significant travel expense, health and safety concerns, or unavoidable scheduling conflicts); contact the courtroom deputy (503-326-8061) to schedule. Judge Hallman waives LR 5-10 and requires no paper copies. The waiver does not apply to documents in the judge’s cases that another judge will consider, unless that judge also waives the rule.

docs.t: Judge Andrew D. Hallman (D. Or.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Andrew D. Hallman, D. Or.. Summary judgment: Seek summary judgment only on issues with no question of material fact or that raise significant dispositive legal issues. Cite the record by paragraph number of affidavits and declarations or by page number of deposition excerpts, and submit all documents in an organized fashion.

docs.t: Judge Andrew D. Hallman (D. Or.) — Settlement conference requirements (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew D. Hallman, D. Or.. Settlement conference requirements (trap): Everyone with settlement authority must attend, including anyone with input on whether to settle, such as a spouse, parent, or other adviser. Before the conference the parties must complete meaningful discovery and exchange at least two cycles of demand and counteroffer covering all material terms. Participation is voluntary unless the assigned judge ordered it, and must be in good faith. Email a Confidential Settlement Memorandum directly to the judge by 12:00 p.m. on the date the order sets. Noncompliance without prior approval may bring sanctions, including the other parties’ costs and attorney fees of attending.

docs.t: Judge Andrew D. Hallman (D. Or.) — Settlement memorandum
docs.x: Judge Andrew D. Hallman, D. Or.. Settlement memorandum: Limit it to 10 pages; attach only key exhibits, and cite record documents (for example, ECF 10 at 3-4) rather than attaching them. Don’t write a summary judgment brief; be candid about weaknesses. Address the three best and three worst facts, legal issues that could change your position, factors making settlement difficult, common goals, negotiation status with each side’s last proposal, fees and costs to date and estimated through trial and appeal, and a realistic settlement range. Undisclosed new claims or defenses may lead to postponement; disclose essential settlement terms beforehand, preferably in written bullet points.

docs.t: Judge Andrew D. Hallman (D. Or.) — Settlement confidentiality
docs.x: Judge Andrew D. Hallman, D. Or.. Settlement confidentiality: Communications are not disclosed outside chambers or to other parties without consent, and confidentiality survives the conference. If the case does not settle, the assigned judge learns nothing more about it.

docs.t: Judge Andrew D. Hallman (D. Or.) — Rule 16 and expedited cases
docs.x: Judge Andrew D. Hallman, D. Or.. Rule 16 and expedited cases: Rule 16 conferences are set after all defendants have answered. Confer under Rule 26(f) beforehand; emailing a joint proposed case management schedule to the courtroom deputy in advance is encouraged. With consent and an agreed expedited schedule, the court sets a case management conference on discovery limits and dispositive motions and will try to set trial within six months of it.

docs.t: Judge Andrew D. Hallman (D. Or.) — Young lawyers and courtroom
docs.x: Judge Andrew D. Hallman, D. Or.. Young lawyers and courtroom: The judge strongly encourages speaking roles for lawyers practicing less than 7 years, especially when they drafted the papers; an experienced attorney may supplement. Under LR 83-14, wireless devices must be silent and nothing may be recorded, including remote proceedings. Give advance notice of technology needs. Pro hac vice counsel and their Oregon counsel should know the Local Rules and the 2013 Federal Bar Association newsletter article “The Integral Role of Local Counsel in the District of Oregon,” which stresses that local counsel must “meaningfully participate” (LR 83-3(a)(1)).

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Armistead (D. Or.) — Judge’s copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Armistead, D. Or.. Judge’s copies (trap): Paper copies are required for any filing totaling more than 10 pages (main document and attachments), within three business days after electronic filing. Put them in a three-ring binder with tabs for all documents and exhibits, printed double-sided with the ECF banner showing docket number and filed date. Deliver to the Clerk’s Office or mail to chambers (Room 927, Hatfield Courthouse, Portland).

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Armistead (D. Or.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Armistead, D. Or.. Discovery disputes (trap): Disputes are resolved informally: request a conference with the judge through the courtroom deputy before moving for any discovery order. If needed, the judge sets a telephonic hearing and requires a joint statement summarizing the dispute. If you expect to need help with a deposition dispute, tell the courtroom deputy the deposition date and time in advance.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Armistead (D. Or.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Armistead, D. Or.. Motions: Oral argument is not set automatically; chambers will contact the parties if argument would help. The court prefers that cited cases be hyperlinked (Section 5 of the CM/ECF User Manual).

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Armistead (D. Or.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Armistead, D. Or.. Summary judgment: Reserve summary judgment for issues with no question of material fact or significant dispositive legal issues. Cite the record by paragraph number of affidavits and declarations or by page number of deposition excerpts.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Armistead (D. Or.) — Rule 16 conference
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Armistead, D. Or.. Rule 16 conference: Set after all defendants have answered or appeared. Confer under LR 16-2(b) and 26-1, and submit the formal joint Rule 26(f) Report and Discovery Plan before the conference, by filing it or emailing it to the courtroom deputy. Be ready to discuss status, dates, and significant issues. Consent to magistrate judge jurisdiction is encouraged, particularly if you want a firm trial date.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Armistead (D. Or.) — Courtroom and pronouns
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Armistead, D. Or.. Courtroom and pronouns: Wireless devices must be silent in the courthouse, and nothing may be recorded, including remote proceedings. Give advance notice of teleconferencing, video display, or other technology needs. Parties and counsel may give their pronouns and honorifics (e.g., Mr., Ms., Mx., Dr.) in writing or orally at conferences, hearings, or trials.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey Armistead (D. Or.) — Contact and pro hac vice
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey Armistead, D. Or.. Contact and pro hac vice: Case questions go to the courtroom deputy (503-326-8061). The proposed-documents email is only for jury instructions and proposed orders under LR 5, not filings. Pro hac vice counsel and their Oregon counsel should know the judge’s preferences and the Local Rules.

docs.t: Judge John V. Acosta (D. Or.) — Scheduling and format
docs.x: Judge John V. Acosta, D. Or.. Scheduling and format: Request a settlement conference, and make all other inquiries, by emailing the courtroom deputy. Conferences are held by Zoom, or in person in Eugene on request. The instructions are to be strictly followed.

docs.t: Judge John V. Acosta (D. Or.) — Who must attend (trap)
docs.x: Judge John V. Acosta, D. Or.. Who must attend (trap): Each party’s decision-maker, with full and final authority to settle without conferring with anyone absent, must attend in person or by Zoom. If a governing body must approve, the attendee must be able to represent that it likely will follow the attendee’s recommendation. The trial attorney and any settlement attorney must participate; an out-of-district trial attorney must attend with the party’s Oregon counsel. Identify every attendee by name and title.

docs.t: Judge John V. Acosta (D. Or.) — Position statement (trap)
docs.x: Judge John V. Acosta, D. Or.. Position statement (trap): Ten pages maximum, single spaced, letter format, standard margins, 12-point font or larger; noncompliant statements are returned. Email it to John_Acosta@ord.uscourts.gov at least five business days before the conference. Address the three best and three worst facts, pivotal legal issues, damages and how calculated (both sides), obstacles, common goals, negotiation status with each side’s last proposal, fees and costs to date and through trial, a realistic settlement range (required, though not your bottom line), and a realistic verdict range. Don’t argue you will surely win summary judgment or trial; be candid. Key exhibits may be attached if reasonable in number and length.

docs.t: Judge John V. Acosta (D. Or.) — Preparation
docs.x: Judge John V. Acosta, D. Or.. Preparation: Agree beforehand on whose turn it is to make the next number and what the prior numbers were. Don’t arrive with a worse number (plaintiff higher, defendant lower) or with new claims or defenses; convey any change well before the day before. Settle the components of economic damages in advance and timely produce relevant discovery. Exchange all material terms, including confidentiality, tax, indemnification, allocation, no-rehire, and non-disparagement provisions, preferably in writing. The paying party must bring enough authority, not a fixed figure set by someone absent; the plaintiff must come with an open mind.

docs.t: Judge John V. Acosta (D. Or.) — Settlement conduct and fees (trap)

The judge retains jurisdiction over the settlement only if the agreement and the final dismissal order specifically provide for it.

docs.x: Judge Darrell A. Clay, N.D. Ohio. Newer-attorney oral argument: Within 7 days after a civil motion is fully briefed, a newer attorney (in practice seven years or less) may file a written Request for Oral Argument stating that the newer attorney will argue the motion. Emergency requests are emailed to WillisNYSDChambers@nysd.uscourts.gov and filed on the docket. Calendar matters: call (212) 805-0244 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. or email chambers. Hand deliveries go to the Court Security Officers at the 500 Pearl Street Worth Street entrance, not to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Jennifer E. Willis (S.D.N.Y.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jennifer E. Willis, S.D.N.Y.. Discovery disputes (trap): Local Rule 37.2 as modified: confer in good faith in person or by telephone, then file a letter motion of up to 3 single-spaced pages stating when the meet-and-confer occurred and requesting a conference. The response is due within 3 business days (same length limit); failing to respond within 3 business days waives any objections. The court tries to resolve disputes without a conference or formal briefing. For disputes during a deposition, continue as far as possible, do not unilaterally terminate it, and then jointly call chambers at (212) 805-0244.

docs.t: Judge Jennifer E. Willis (S.D.N.Y.) — Pre-motion letters
docs.x: Judge Jennifer E. Willis, S.D.N.Y.. Pre-motion letters: Meet and confer on a briefing schedule first; pre-motion letters must propose one and are required for motions returnable before or referred to Judge Willis. Exempt: pro hac vice, cases with an incarcerated pro se party, reconsideration, new trial, in limine, Fed. R. App. P. 4(a)(4)(A) motions, recusal, habeas petitions, orders to show cause, and Rule 12(b)(6) motions in lieu of an answer. Responses are due within 3 business days.

docs.t: Judge Jennifer E. Willis (S.D.N.Y.) — Briefs and oral argument (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jennifer E. Willis, S.D.N.Y.. Briefs and oral argument (trap): Memoranda are limited to 8,750 words and replies to 3,500 words; memoranda of 10 pages or more need tables of contents and authorities (not counted). No sur-replies without permission. All filings must be searchable PDFs, and cite Westlaw for unreported cases where possible. Request oral argument on the moving papers or by letter. A request is more likely to be granted if a lawyer who graduated law school within the previous 5 years will argue.

docs.t: Judge Jennifer E. Willis (S.D.N.Y.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jennifer E. Willis, S.D.N.Y.. Summary judgment (trap): At the meet-and-confer before the pre-motion letter, the parties should prepare a joint submission of all undisputed facts, or submit a letter explaining why they should be relieved of that obligation. Briefs must set out the facts relied on rather than just citing the Rule 56.1 statements.

docs.t: Judge Jennifer E. Willis (S.D.N.Y.) — Excel sheets for damages and fees (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jennifer E. Willis, S.D.N.Y.. Excel sheets for damages and fees (trap): For inquests on damages, attorney’s fees motions, FLSA damages, and IDEA reimbursements, the movant must email an Excel sheet of the calculations to chambers (copying all parties) when filing or within 14 days after referral, even if already submitted to the district judge, and file a letter stating when it was emailed.

docs.t: Judge Jennifer E. Willis (S.D.N.Y.) — Sealing
docs.x: Judge Jennifer E. Willis, S.D.N.Y.. Sealing: Redaction or sealing based on a confidentiality designation requires a public letter motion explaining the specific reasons, with the sealed document filed under seal and related to it, the proposed redacted version filed publicly, and an unredacted copy with redactions highlighted filed under seal. Deadlines are not stayed: file the redacted version, serve unredacted papers, and give chambers unredacted courtesy copies.

docs.t: Judge Jennifer E. Willis (S.D.N.Y.) — Case management and discovery forms
docs.x: Judge Jennifer E. Willis, S.D.N.Y.. Case management and discovery forms: File the Proposed Case Management Plan and Report of Rule 26(f) Meeting on the judge’s template 1 week before the initial conference (pro se cases use the pro se template); lead counsel are expected to attend. Junior lawyers are invited to speak at conferences. Proposed protective orders that differ from the model must attach a comparison to the model. Parties may use the model ESI Plan. The party ordering a hearing transcript must email a copy to chambers. Electronic device requests: email the court form to chambers, copying opposing counsel, by close of business the day before the appearance.

docs.t: Judge Jennifer E. Willis (S.D.N.Y.) — Settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jennifer E. Willis, S.D.N.Y.. Settlement conferences (trap): Seven days before the pre-conference call, email chambers a joint settlement letter (3 pages max: negotiation history, each side’s valuation and rationale, authority, other helpful facts), each counsel’s Acknowledgment Form, and a jointly prepared Settlement Conference Form; optional ex parte letters must be under 1 page. The forms themselves say “no later than three days before” the call. Binder courtesy copies if letter and exhibits exceed 10 pages. Plaintiff must make (or renew) a demand at least 10 days before the conference, and defendant must respond at least 3 days before the pre-conference call, held about a week ahead with counsel only. Parties attend in person with full decision-making authority (including each insurer, excess carriers unless excused at least 1 week ahead); telephone attendance only on a letter

docs.t: Judge Jennifer E. Willis (S.D.N.Y.) — Pretrial and trial (consent cases)
docs.x: Judge Jennifer E. Willis, S.D.N.Y.. Pretrial and trial (consent cases): Joint Pretrial Order due within 30 days after discovery closes, including witness lists with time estimates, exhibits with objections, stipulations, a demonstrative exchange schedule, voir dire, jury instructions, and verdict sheet; default rule is notice of witness order 48 hours before trial. Pro se cases use separate sworn Pretrial Statements. Each party emails pre-marked exhibits to chambers (not ECF) and submits one hard copy in a tabbed three-ring binder.

docs.t: Judge Jennifer E. Willis (S.D.N.Y.) — Criminal matters
docs.x: Judge Jennifer E. Willis, S.D.N.Y.. Criminal matters: Warrants, pen registers, NDOs, and other applications go to WillisCriminalDuty@nysd.uscourts.gov, with the times the agent and AUSA are available. Plea papers (charging instrument, plea agreement, elements, and penalties) are due by email at least 24 hours before the plea; misdemeanor sentencing submissions at least 2 weeks before sentencing.

docs.t: Judge Judith C. McCarthy (S.D.N.Y.) — Scope and consent
docs.x: Judge Judith C. McCarthy, S.D.N.Y.. Scope and consent: These practices apply to matters within the district judge’s order of reference or to cases before Judge McCarthy for all purposes under 28 U.S.C. § 636(c); otherwise the district judge’s practices govern. They do not override statutory or rule-based motion deadlines (e.g., Fed. R. Civ. P. 50, 52, 54, 59, 60; Fed. R. App. P. 4). Civil consent cases get firm trial dates, unlikely to move for criminal trials. White Plains courthouse, Courtroom 325.

docs.t: Judge Judith C. McCarthy (S.D.N.Y.) — Letters and contact (trap)
docs.x: Judge Judith C. McCarthy, S.D.N.Y.. Letters and contact (trap): Communicate by letter filed on ECF, up to 5 pages excluding exhibits; discovery letters are limited by the case’s discovery order. Responsive letters must cite the docket number of the letter answered. Do not send counsel-to-counsel correspondence. Courtesy copies are required for letters over 10 pages including exhibits. If an ECF letter needs immediate attention, telephone chambers to flag it. Phone calls to chambers ((914) 390-4124) are permitted; faxes and emails are not without prior approval (faxes limited to 5 pages).

docs.t: Judge Judith C. McCarthy (S.D.N.Y.) — Adjournments and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Judith C. McCarthy, S.D.N.Y.. Adjournments and extensions (trap): File letter motions stating the original date, number of prior requests, whether they were granted or denied, and whether the adversary consents (and its reasons if not). Attach a proposed Revised Scheduling Order (business days only) if other dates are affected. Requests are due 48 hours before the conference or deadline, absent an emergency; for anything within 48 hours or otherwise urgent, also call chambers.

docs.t: Judge Judith C. McCarthy (S.D.N.Y.) — Pre-motion conferences and discovery
docs.x: Judge Judith C. McCarthy, S.D.N.Y.. Pre-motion conferences and discovery: Discovery motions follow Local Civil Rule 37.2 (informal conference first) with strict Rule 37(a)(1) meet-and-confer; be ready to state the time, place, and duration of the meeting and the counsel involved. A pre-motion conference is required for all other motions except pro hac vice, reargument or reconsideration, Rule 11(c)(2), and motions already on a briefing schedule. File a letter of up to 3 pages; the response (up to 3 pages) is due within 3 business days.

docs.t: Judge Judith C. McCarthy (S.D.N.Y.) — Briefs and courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Judith C. McCarthy, S.D.N.Y.. Briefs and courtesy copies (trap): Courtesy copies of all motion papers, marked as such, securely bound and tabbed, and bearing ECF proof of filing, go to chambers when the papers are served. Memoranda are limited to 8,750 words and replies to 3,500 words, with a word-count certificate; briefs of 3,500 words or more need a table of contents. Handwritten or typed pro se briefs: 25 pages, replies 10. Use 12-point type (10-point footnotes), 1-inch margins, and double spacing. Request oral argument by letter when filing your papers; the court decides whether to hear it.

docs.t: Judge Judith C. McCarthy (S.D.N.Y.) — Sealing
docs.x: Judge Judith C. McCarthy, S.D.N.Y.. Sealing: Sealing or redaction requires a public motion or letter motion under Standing Order 19-mc-00583 and ECF Rules Section 6, with the proposed sealed document filed under seal and related to it, and for redactions both a public redacted version and a sealed highlighted unredacted version. Send unredacted courtesy copies to chambers when the motion is filed. Under the model protective order, a confidentiality designation creates no presumption of sealing; it also includes a Rule 502(d) non-waiver clause and requires return or destruction within 30 days after final judgment.

docs.t: Judge Judith C. McCarthy (S.D.N.Y.) — Pretrial filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Judith C. McCarthy, S.D.N.Y.. Pretrial filings (trap): Joint pretrial orders only if directed; when required they include Rule 26(a)(3) material plus jurisdiction statements, any Rule 48 consent to a nonunanimous verdict, itemized damages, a joint statement for jurors, witness and exhibit objections, deposition or video testimony, equipment needs, and anticipated in limine motions. Thirty days before trial each party files witness and exhibit lists, objections, in limine motions (responses 21 days before trial), and requests to charge, voir dire, and verdict sheet (jury) or proposed findings and conclusions (nonjury); email Word copies to chambers. Exhibit and deposition-designation binders go to the court and each party 5 court days before the final pretrial conference.
